mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenue growth and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing wage growth and consumer spending, which in turn pressures corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of UNRATE > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when INDPRO m/m < -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and personal savings (RSAFS) signals robust household balance sheets and housing demand, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when HOUST and RSAFS correlation exceeds 0.6 for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods when PAYEMS > 12-mo MA for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below -1% combined with a simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% signals a deepening economic recession, which causes a pronounced drop in S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 YoY < -1% and UNRATE > 4%.
